rules: Approve when the vote directly tests the specific commitment.

A vote on a whole bill counts, in both directions, when the promised item was a central, widely reported provision (H.R.1's tax-cut extension, Medicaid and SNAP cuts, Planned Parenthood funding ban, border wall and Border Patrol/ICE money).

Show as 'shown, not scored' (related vote) when the vote bears on the promise but a kept/broken call would rest on a contested reading: Social Security and Medicare (H.R.1 didn't change benefits), abortion-rights promises tested by the Born-Alive bill, child tax credit and middle-class tax promises (H.R.1 changed both in part), SALT repeal, and 'work across the aisle' promises.

Test promises to cut spending against the Rescissions Act of 2025 (H.R. 4), a direct $9 billion spending cut; H.R.1, whose net effect on spending depends on the baseline, is shown as a related vote, not scored.
Reject slogans and section headings, statements about past votes, text dating from earlier races that the 2024 vote can't test, and quotes our archive can't show.
Reject later duplicates of the same quote.
Score a promise only with votes that directly test it; show other relevant votes as related, not scored.

The Laken Riley Act (detention of immigrants charged with crimes) scores promises about immigration enforcement, deportation or ending illegal immigration. For promises that only say 'secure the border', it is a related vote.
A promise is aligned when every scored vote matches it, not aligned when every scored vote goes against it, and mixed otherwise. 'Present' and 'Not voting' are not counted.
A vote counts toward at most one promise per member, so a single bill cannot stack up a member's score.
A member's score (promises aligned out of promises tested) is shown only once at least 3 of their promises have been tested.

promises.quote: This starts with raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour, supporting workers’ right to organize and join a union, passing the Protecting the Right to Organize (PRO) Act, increasing support for our small businesses, and repealing the Trump tax cuts for the wealthiest one-percent.
She will also use her business experience to get Washington’s spending under control.

George supports responsible cryptocurrency regulations that protect consumers while fostering innovation and competition in the digital asset space, and establish a framework to support American leadership in this growing sector.

We have laws on the books— we must ensure that our nation’s current immigration laws are enforced, immigration programs work properly, and that we provide the resources for law enforcement officials to get their jobs done.
We must also invest in our Border Patrol agents and law enforcement officers.
